contributions.statement: For Java unit-test generation, replace LLM compile-repair loops with rule-based static repair, which cut generation time 51-69% and tokens 67-84% at similar or better compile rates.
contributions.evidence: Table 4 (QC-32B): 1,836 s / 203k tokens vs 3,768-5,924 s / 1.09-1.26M; Table 7 swap. Audit: quality half is thin, since repair rules delete unbindable references and add fallback assertions, which inflates compile/pass metrics; single model, closed benchmark.
relative_to: P17 static analysis in the loop

contributions.statement: Stamp the test-class skeleton (imports, runner/extension annotations, mocks, setup) from framework templates for JUnit 5, Mockito or Spring Boot Test and ask the LLM only for test bodies.
contributions.evidence: Table 3 ablation: w/o skeleton line coverage -16.37; single model (Qwen2.5-Coder-32B), deltas without variance; small/dated models only.

reason: Java industrial evidence for moving scaffolding and compile repair out of the LLM. Cost gains are robust; quality gains are partly metric artifacts and must be checked with mutation score.
